The team's head coach was [[Dino Gaudio]]. The team played its home games in the [[Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum]] in [[Winston-Salem, North Carolina]], and was a member of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). On January 19, the Deacons took the top spot in both the ESPN/USA Today coaches poll and the Associated Press poll, making it the second time in program history a Wake Forest team was number one in the country. Wake Forest finished the regular season with a record of 24–5, and 11–5 in the ACC, which tied them with [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. The Demon Deacons received the number two seed in the [[2009 ACC men's basketball tournament]] in a tiebreaker over Duke because of their victory against number one seed North Carolina. ==Preseason==
